questions.question:
**Directions: **Read each sentence to find out whether there is any grammatical error or idiomatic error in it. The error will be in one part of the sentence. The number of that part is the answer.

After a complaint was filed, (A)/ police teams was given the photograph (B)/ of the accused from the CCTV footage (C)/ recorded at the hotel (D)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"B". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **'police teams was given' **is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Since **'teams' **is plural, the verb should also be in a plural form.
 
• The correct form is **'were given' **to maintain subject-verb agreement.
 
• For plural subjects, the plural form of the verb is necessary to form a grammatically correct sentence in English.
 
• Therefore, part B of the sentence contains the grammatical error.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Options 1 (A), 3 (C), and 4 (D) do not contain any grammatical or idiomatic error.
 
• Grammatically, all these parts of the sentence are correct and logically sound.

questions.question:
Select the word that needs to be changed to make the sentence correct.

He loves to reads books about history in his spare time.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "reads".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the sentence the error lies in the use of the verb** "reads."**
 
• In English language grammar, when we use the base verb after 'to,' it is always in its simplest form.
 
• Here**, "reads" **should be **"read."**
 
• The construction **'to'** followed by a** basic verb form** is known as the** infinitive,** used commonly after verbs like 'love,' 'like,' 'hate,' etc.
 
• So, the correct form of the verb in this sentence should be **"read" rather than "reads."**
 
• This change would correctly express that **he loves the activity of reading books.**

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 2".**

• **Probability **is a synonym of feasibility because it also refers to the likelihood or chance of something occurring. (किसी चीज़ के घटित होने की संभावना)
 
 
• **Example**: *There is a high probability of rain tomorrow, so you might want to carry an umbrella.*

• **Impropriety **means improper behaviour or conduct. (अनुचित व्यवहार या आचरण)

questions.question: The manager took __unilateral__ decision. What is the meaning of underlined word?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **individual.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"unilateral"** in the context of a decision refers to an action or decision made by a single entity or person without agreement or consultation with others. (एक तरफा)

 
 
• **Example:** It seems that unilateral nuclear disarmament is back on the agenda.
 
 
 
• A unilateral decision is an individual decision, because it is decided by alone, without any consultation or agreement from others. It's about a single individual taking action.
 
• **Individual: **considered separately rather than as part of a group (समूह से अलग; अकेला)
 
 
• **Example:** The reason he was chosen was that he has a very individual style
 
 
 
• As we can see, the meaning of **'unilateral'** is **'individual'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **individual**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the** meanings **of the other options.

 
• **Collective: **Collective is formed or done by people acting as a group. It's the opposite of unilateral since a collective decision involves a group's input or consensus. (सामूहिक)

 
 
• **Example:** We need a collective effort to cut down litter.
 
 
 
• **Multilateral:** Multilateral refers to a decision, agreement, or action taken by multiple parties, typically more than two. It's different from unilateral as unilateral involves only one party while multilateral involves many parties. (बहुपक्षीय)
 
 
• **Example:** The multilateral talks lasted a long while.
 
 
 
• **Multiple:** Multiple means having several parts, elements, or members. In the context of decisions, it doesn't align with the concept of unilateral since multiple would mean involving several decisions or factors. (एकाधिक)
 
 
• **Example:** By this time next year expect the percentage to be a multiple of that.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

It is expected that this police power will only apply to air and (sea routes between the Great Britain and the Northern Ireland).

options.text: Sea routes across the Great Britain and Northern Ireland
Sea routes across the Great Britain and the Northern Ireland
Sea routes between Great Britain and Northern Ireland

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3'** i.e. **'Sea routes between Great Britain and Northern Ireland'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The use of **'the'** before *Great Britain* and* Northern Ireland*, is wrong.
 
• **'The'** is used before the name of countries which are a group of islands or the country that contains a political title in its name.
 
 
• **For Example** - The Bahamas, The United Kingdom, The Czech Republic, etc.
 
 
 
• On the other hand names of the countries like India, **Northern Ireland**, **Great Britain**, etc. do not take **'the'** before them.
 
 
• For Example -
 
 
• I am from** the India** (**Not Correct**)
 
• I am from **India** (**Correct**)
 
 
 
 
 
• So, according to the rule, the correct form of the bracketed portion is **'****Sea routes between Great Britain and Northern Ireland'.**

Therefore, the correct answer is **'Sea routes between Great Britain and Northern Ireland'.**

**The correct sentence is:** It is expected that this police power will only apply to air and **sea routes between Great Britain and Northern Ireland__**.

questions.question:
**In the following items, each passage consists of six sentences. The first sentence (S1) and the final sentence (S6) are given. The middle four sentences in each have been removed and jumbled up. These are labelled P, Q, R and S. You are required to find out the proper sequence of the four sentences and mark accordingly on the Answer Sheet. **

S1: Life is a gift of God to man. 

P: What an invaluable gift! 

Q: Every morning He fills 24 hours in wallets of each of us and never asks questions. 

R: The other is time. 

S: Irrespective of these gifts, we grumble. 

S6: Oh Lord! What fools we mortals are?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**PRQS**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sentence **S1** mentions that life is a gift of God to man.
 
• Sentence **P** describes this gift as invaluable.
 
• Sentence **R** explains that God fills 24 hours into the wallets of each person every morning and never asks questions.
 
• Sentence **Q** mentions that, despite these gifts, people grumble.
 
• Sentence **S** states that we are fools for doing this.
 
• Sentence **S6** confirms this sentiment with the exclamation, "Oh Lord! What fools we mortals are?"
 
• When the sentences are put in this order, they form a coherent and logical paragraph about **the gifts that God gives to people and how we often take them for granted and complain despite their value**.

Thus, ***option 2*** is the correct answer.

**Correct paragraph**__: ***S1** Life is a gift of God to man. **P** What an invaluable gift! R The other is time. **Q** Every morning He fills 24 hours in wallets of each of us and never asks questions. **S** Irrespective of these gifts, we grumble. **S6** Oh Lord! What fools we mortals are? *

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

Frank has being making / the rounds, advancing a theory / that I believe is not without merit.

options.text: that I believe is not without merit

questions.solution:
The erroneous part is '**Frank has being making**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here, '**Frank has been making**' should be used instead of '**Frank has being making**'.
 
• The **perfect tenses **(past, present, and future) are formed with a form of 'have' and the past participle form of the main verb (had finished, has visited, have returned) for the **active voice.**
 
• The given sentence is in the** passive voice.**
 
• To use the** passive voice**, the word been is placed between the two (had been finished, has been visited, have been returned). 
 
 
• *Example: The reports** have been written.***
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** ***Frank has been making** the rounds, advancing a theory that I believe is not without merit.*

We were invited to lunch with local __bigwigs__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**small fry"**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bigwigs** is a slang term that refers to important or influential people, especially those who hold positions of power or authority. (बिगविग्स एक कठबोली शब्द है जो महत्वपूर्ण या प्रभावशाली लोगों को संदर्भित करता है, विशेष रूप से वे जो सत्ता या अधिकार के पदों पर रहते हैं।)

 
 
• **Example: **The conference was attended by bigwigs from all over the country, including the CEO of a major corporation and several high-ranking politicians.
 
 

**Let's see the meanings of the given words**__

__
 
• **Mangers **are containers or troughs used to hold feed for livestock, especially horses and cows. (नांद कंटेनर या गर्त होते हैं जिनका उपयोग पशुओं, विशेष रूप से घोड़ों और गायों के लिए चारा रखने के लिए किया जाता है।)

 
 
• **Example: ***The horses were fed twice a day, with fresh hay and grain placed in the **mangers** for them to eat.*
 
 
 
• **Small fry** is a colloquial term that refers to young, inexperienced, or unimportant people or things. (स्मॉल फ्राई एक बोलचाल का शब्द है जो युवा, अनुभवहीन, या महत्वहीन लोगों या चीजों को संदर्भित करता है।)
 
 
• **Example:** *The big corporations dominate the industry, leaving little room for the **small fry** to compete.*
 
 
 
• **Riff-raff** is a derogatory term for people who are considered to be undesirable or disreputable. (रिफ-रफ उन लोगों के लिए अपमानजनक शब्द है जिन्हें अवांछनीय या विवादित माना जाता है।)
 
 
• **Example:** *a group of protesters as "**riff-raff"** if they disagree with their beliefs or actions, or someone might use the term to describe a group of people who are considered poor or lower class.*
 
 
 
• **Novices **are people who are new or inexperienced in a particular field or activity. (नौसिखिए वे लोग होते हैं जो किसी विशेष क्षेत्र या गतिविधि में नए या अनुभवहीन होते हैं।)
 
 
• **Example: ***The team of **novices** worked hard to learn the ropes of their new job.*
 
 

According to the meanings of the given words,* the correct answer is **Option 2, i.e.,small fry.***

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

To breast the tape

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"To breast the tape" **is an idiomatic expression originating from competitive running.
 
• In a race, **a tape is stretched **across the finish line.

• So, it essentially **means** "To win a race".

• **To shut someone’s mouth **- This phrase generally means to cause someone to stop speaking, often by making them feel guilty or embarrassed. It does not have a similar meaning to "To breast the tape". (किसी का मूंह बंद करना).
 
• **To create problems** - This phrase means to cause difficulties or obstacles. (समस्याएँ पैदा करना).
 
• **To bring joy** - This phrase means to make someone feel happy or satisfied. Although winning a race can bring joy, this phrase is not specifically equivalent to "To breast the tape".(खुशी लाना).

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence is given in Direct speech. Out of the four alternatives choose the one which best expresses the sentence in Indirect Speech.**

David said to me, “How can I get to higher places in life?”

options.text: David told me How could I get to higher places in life.
David asked me whether I could get to higher places in life.
David asked me how he could get to higher places in life.
David asked me how I could get to higher places in life?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option** **3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let us begin by identifying the kind of sentence. It is an **interrogative** **sentence**. (Wh-Question)
 
• The reporting verb ‘said to’ should be changed as ‘**asked**’ in indirect speech.
 
• Following that, we need to remove the commas and inverted commas as we change it into an indirect speech.
 
• The Question is changed into **assertive form** and is simply placed after the reporting verb.
 
• The question mark is also removed.

**Correct answer:** *“David asked me how he could get to higher places in life.”* [IMAGE: https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-l3avs6cvGwQG409IOPNorWcR7aNklXzzcxSpHiSIKqYjG6LQUNmUmzJa99JZxqc-mH6mOdCH_KJr0bjR6CaZdK8Xxf2emPl_IELD8Xzs5BdLt9hAT_XfgMqcIdIY21qZvpprmoz] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

When changing a direct speech to indirect speech:

 
• The words of the speaker are not enclosed in inverted commas.
 
• The conjunction ‘that’ will not be used. (In case of interrogative sentence)
 
• To make an indirect speech of Wh -Questions, The Question is changed into assertive form and is simply placed after the reporting verb.
 
• To make an indirect speech of YES/NO-Questions, if or whether will be used.
 
• The question mark is also removed.
 
• e.g., DIRECT: He said to me, “Will you help me?”

 INDIRECT: He asked me if I would help him.

 
• DIRECT: He said to me, “Why are you late?”

 INDIRECT: He asked me why I was late.

__
